claims.text: THE TIER 1 PHYSICAL ANCHOR AGAINST THE PROPULSION CLAIM. The NIST Chemistry WebBook gives mercury, CAS 7439-97-6, a melting point of 234.31 K (Marsh, 1987, uncertainty assigned by TRC 0.005 K), a triple point of 234.3 K, and a boiling point of 629.81 K.

claims.source: Reasoning over the NIST phase change data for mercury and slide 72 of the 1998 presentation; research/leads/verified-tr3b-2026-09-18.md section 6.2
claims.text: Stated inference, and it is a short one. 150 K is 84 K below mercury's melting point of 234.31 K at one atmosphere. Mercury's melting curve has a positive slope, so a pressure of 250,000 atmospheres raises the melting point rather than lowering it, putting the material further into the solid region and not closer to a gas. A plasma is an ionised gas. The specification therefore describes a solid and calls it a plasma, and it does so before any question of superconductivity, rotation or gravity is reached.

claims.source: Reasoning over slide 72 of the 1998 presentation; research/leads/verified-tr3b-2026-09-18.md section 6.2
claims.text: Stated inference, second order. The presentation forecloses the usual defence itself: 'Do not misunderstand. This is not antigravity... The MFD creates a disruption of the Earth's gravitational field upon the mass within the circular accelerator.' A magnetic field acting on gravitational mass is not a mechanism in any physical literature opened here, and the presentation gives no field strength, no power budget and no mass figure against which the claimed 89 per cent reduction could be checked. There is nothing in it to test, which is itself the finding.

desc: The TR-3B is a CLAIMED craft for whose existence no record has been opened, and the board carries it as a claim and not as an object: every substantive description of it descends from a single named man's speaking script, which he copyrighted himself in August 1998 and which attributes the sighting itself to an unnamed friend. Everything on this node is therefore a description of a claim. One artefact carries that description and is why the node exists: the 62 page transcript headed 'Presentation to IUFOR by Edgar Rothshild Fouche / Copyright Aug. 1998 / Fouche Media Associates', in which slides 69 to 72 give the craft its designation and code name Astra, place it at Papoose, attribute it to 'the Top Secret, Aurora Program with SDI and black budget monies', name the National Reconnaissance Office, the NSA and the CIA as its funders and taskers, name Sandia and Livermore as developers of its propulsion, and specify 'a circular, plasma filled accelerator ring called the Magnetic Field Disrupter' running a 'mercury based' plasma 'pressurized at 250,000 atmospheres at a temperature of 150 degrees Kelvin and accelerated to 50,000 rpm'. THE DOCUMENT CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT THE SIZE OF THE CRAFT TWO SLIDES APART: slide 69 says 'The operational model is 600 feet across' and slide 70 says 'The 200 feet Prototype & the 300 feet Operational TR-3Bs are Code named Astra'. Both sentences are in the same document, in sequence, and nobody outside it has to adjudicate that. Three further things constrain this node. The presentation was given in the same summer as, and in order to promote, a book the Library of Congress catalogues as science fiction, LCCN 98002961, genre heading 'Science fiction.', subject 'Alien abduction - Fiction'. The propulsion specification is refuted by the freezing point of its own stated working fluid: NIST gives mercury a melting point of 234.31 K, and 150 K is 84 K below that. And the presentation's companion craft, the 'SR-75 Penetrator', is the name of a Testors plastic model kit of a speculative aircraft sold from 1993, five years earlier, about which the Air Force told the Baltimore Sun 'such a plane does not exist'.

Where the ARV thread's sizes drifted across three documents over thirty-four years, this one disagrees with itself inside a single afternoon's script.

dossier.narrative:
The case for a node carrying a claim with no evidence behind it is the same case the ARV node made, and this cluster tests it harder. Before this build the board carried DARPA, Northrop, the USAF, Groom Lake and Edwards, and carried nothing for the aircraft those four names are most often attached to in public. A reader arriving with the TR-3B in mind found nothing, which reads as the board having no view. It has a view, and this node states it.

The strongest single fact here is a cataloguing decision. The narrative enters the world attached to a book that the national library shelves as a novel. The second strongest is that the originating document contradicts itself two slides apart, giving the craft as '600 feet across' and then as 'the 300 feet Operational TR-3Bs'. The third is physical: the claimed mercury plasma is specified at 150 degrees Kelvin, and NIST gives mercury's melting point as 234.31 K, so the substance would be a solid at the stated temperature. The fourth is prior art: 'SR-75 Penetrator' is the designation of a Testor Corporation model kit marketed from 1993, about which the Air Force publicly said it was not modelled on anything that exists, and it reappears in the 1998 script as inside knowledge.

The documents Fouche published as corroboration were opened in full, fifteen legible pages. They are decorations, training certificates, performance reports and one 1984 personnel letter. There is no DD-214, no clearance record and no programme document among them, and the page presented as a 'SAC/DARPA Classified Document' carries no classification marking and is signed by a technical sergeant in the Directorate of Assignments, Deputy Chief of Staff for Personnel. Fouche applied the redactions himself and says so in his own caption.

One document genuinely earns its place on the other side, and the node carries it as such rather than burying it. An AF Form 77a of 24 August 1979 records Technical Sergeant Fouche assigned on temporary duty to AFFTC Detachment 3, Nellis AF Range, from 1 June to 14 August 1979, and it is the sceptic's own published reference work that identifies DET 3 AFFTC as Groom Lake. The same form then limits itself: it says his duties there were verified via a separate report, and that report is not in the file. That is the most interesting single page in the collection and it is the reason the man has a node at all.

What this cluster does not settle is the craft. Nothing here is evidence that a TR-3B exists. Every node is a node about a claim, the hub says so in its first sentence, and the case against is wired in as edges like any other.
openQuestions: Whether Edgar Fouche ever stood at an International UFO Congress podium. The contemporaneous February 1998 programme does not list him, and the August 1998 attribution rests on the header of his own document. The venue and date are softer than the literature assumes.
How the TR-3B actually appears in Alien Rapture: The Chosen. The book was not opened, so nothing here asserts its contents beyond the Library of Congress cataloguing of it.

The alleged recorded confession by Fouche. The forum thread said to hold it returned HTTP 522, and the one account that was opened says its own screenshot was unreadable. No confession is in evidence anywhere, and the board should stop repeating that one exists until someone produces it.
The FOIA return said to bear on his service record was not opened, so nothing is asserted about what it returned.
Any official record, of any kind, using the string 'TR-3B'. None was found.
dossier.whatItIs: A claimed triangular aircraft, called the TR-3B and often the TR-3B 'Astra', said to be a black-programme craft using a mercury-based plasma ring for propulsion. No record of its existence has been opened. The entire account descends from one named man, Edgar Fouche, in a copyrighted 62-page presentation transcript dated August 1998, given to promote a novel he had written with Brad Steiger. The Library of Congress catalogues that novel, Alien Rapture: The Chosen, under LCCN 98002961 with the genre heading 'Science fiction', the subject heading 'Alien abduction - Fiction' and the class PS3556, American fiction. The presentation is the artefact this node is built on, and it is why the node exists, not evidence that the craft does.
dossier.whyImplicated: It is on this map as the second worked example of the rule the board adopted on 18 September 2026: the thing claimed about is a node in its own right, and it is the hub every claimant runs into, the case against included. The TR-3B is one of the most repeated craft claims in the entire subject and the board carried nothing for it, while carrying the sceptical literature, the real black programmes of the period and the contractor estate it is attributed to. Its edges are deliberately mixed: the originating claimant, the documents that carry his account, the site that hosts them, the aerospace historian who took his documents apart, a 1993 commercial model kit whose designations reappear in his script as inside knowledge, and a real declassified stealth demonstrator of the right period whose actual shape is nothing like the claim. Its degree means a lot is claimed here. It does not mean any of it is true, and the tier on each edge says which is which.

timeline.label: The most-reproduced black triangle photograph is confessed as a hoax on Belgian television
timeline.text: Robert Sheaffer records that on 26 July 2011 the Belgian broadcaster RTL carried the photographer's confession about the Petit-Rechain image of the 1989-90 Belgian wave: 'The UFO of Petit-Rechain is not a spaceship from a distant galaxy but a panel of painted styrofoam with three spots affixed', and, from the maker, 'One has managed to fool the whole world with a silly model made of styrofoam.' Fouche's 1998 presentation had attached his craft to 'the country of Belgium' at slide 6. This does not touch the eyewitness reports and it decides nothing about Fouche; it records that the visual corpus the claim borrows plausibility from has a confessed hoax at its centre.
